requirements.requirement: opsadmin user exists on node1 with the exact specified ed25519 public key installed as an authorized SSH key
requirements.summary: cmd-10b560d1d4ab47f3 confirms opsadmin did not previously exist. cmd-2bc100824b14484b created the user and installed the exact specified key into /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with 700/600 perms and correct ownership. cmd-7eb1a7a8d3c843d1 confirms SELinux context, permissions, and the key content as opsadmin. After a temporary test-key addition for verification, cmd-7fa186bde0a84e61 restored authorized_keys to contain exactly the required key. Post-restart, cmd-fa49b02e82994241 confirms the user and the single required key are still present.

requirements.requirement: SSH on node1 requires key-based authentication (password and interactive auth disabled, pubkey auth enabled and functional)
requirements.summary: cmd-b768283ddd314c46/cmd-9d6fbce88a294bee added a drop-in disabling PasswordAuthentication and KbdInteractiveAuthentication while enabling PubkeyAuthentication, validated with sshd -t and sshd -T. cmd-1ddc19f3c4ff4300 reloaded sshd successfully. Functional verification: cmd-6b205138b41b4d35 shows password/keyboard-interactive auth attempt rejected (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic only offered), and cmd-efff54d203144bdd shows pubkey auth actually succeeds with a temporary test key. Post-restart, cmd-fa49b02e82994241 and cmd-c340a7937e784f42 reconfirm the same sshd -T settings and reject password auth, demonstrating the configuration persisted through a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: cmd-946768579b1c4aca captures pre-restart boot_id (bf4e9cbb...), uptime, active sshd, opsadmin existence, and key-only settings. cmd-0dda35b0485b4d93 triggers and acknowledges the reboot; cmd-37edb0ef83424948 and cmd-80c4191551dc461e show connection timeouts during the disruption; cmd-8d857d353ad74650 shows reconnection with a new boot_id (424ccd20...). cmd-fa49b02e82994241 and cmd-c340a7937e784f42 confirm recovered sshd, user, key, and auth settings post-restart. This is cross-checked against the fixed global boot-identity observations (before_prepare = bf4e9cbb..., after_executor = 424ccd20...), which match exactly.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating opsadmin with the exact specified public key and enforcing key-based-only SSH authentication — are directly demonstrated with functional evidence (password auth rejected, pubkey auth succeeds) both before and after a full reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly with a verified boot-identity change cross-checked against fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: Data/cluster-state recovery is not applicable to this single-node SSH configuration task, so that portion of the restart protocol has no distinct evidence beyond service and file state.

The two sequential writes to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf (cmd-b768283ddd314c46 then cmd-9d6fbce88a294bee) are treated as one converging configuration action rather than two independent mutations, since only the final content persisted and both writes targeted the same file for the same stated purpose.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline reviewed chronologically. All state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: user/key creation (cmd-2bc100824b14484b), SELinux context fix (cmd-7eb1a7a8d3c843d1, restorecon), sshd drop-in creation/edit (cmd-b768283ddd314c46 then refined by cmd-9d6fbce88a294bee, converging on the same target file to reach the final required state), sshd reload (cmd-1ddc19f3c4ff4300), a temporary test-key addition for functional pubkey verification (cmd-efff54d203144bdd) fully reverted by cmd-7fa186bde0a84e61 (authorized_keys restored to exactly the required key, test key files removed), and the reboot (cmd-0dda35b0485b4d93) which served the independent restart-evidence protocol. No abandoned files, failed services, or damaged package state are visible in the after_executor snapshot versus before_prepare (failed-services empty in both, package-health clean in both). /tmp/reboot.log appearing in after_executor is an expected artifact of the reboot command itself, not unmanaged executor residue. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were identified.
